candidate_gap: Regional demand growth vs peak-load development
what_literature_establishes: Regional annual consumption and its drivers are well modelled to 2019 (elasticities, structural trends, climate sensitivity of energy).
what_remains_unresolved: Regional monthly load is already forecast from the same KAPSARC series (L31), so descriptives are not new. Still unexamined: regional peak-month structure and load factor as inputs to a supply-side alignment assessment.
why_it_matters: Capacity planning is sized on peak, not energy; regions differ in load composition (industrial East vs residential West).
can_public_data_investigate: Partly: KAPSARC monthly max/avg/min load by region 2009-2019 (index-verified, not downloaded).
confidence: Medium (abstract-level review; monthly peak series not yet inspected)
verdict: Not a standalone gap (downgraded after L31); use only as the demand baseline for G2/G3

candidate_gap: Geographic alignment of renewable deployment with regional demand
what_literature_establishes: Siting studies are resource/land-suitability driven (GIS-MCDA); none found that compares the ACTUAL project pipeline with regional demand.
what_remains_unresolved: Ex-post, public-data comparison of where projects are vs where (peak) load is; inter-regional transfer implications.
why_it_matters: Location determines transmission needs and whether capacity serves the region whose peak is growing.
can_public_data_investigate: Yes for capacity geography (KAPSARC tracker, GEM coordinates); demand side limited to 2019 (monthly peak) and 2023 (annual energy by admin region).
confidence: Medium - no study found in 17 searches; but utility-internal studies (L12) likely cover it with non-public data
verdict: Plausible gap in the PUBLIC literature; must not be claimed as first-ever given L12

what_literature_establishes: Formal ELCC exists only for one SOA mini-grid (2015). National CEMs treat RE firm capacity as an assumption; results are sensitive to it (up to 41% more batteries).
what_remains_unresolved: Location-specific, transparent peak-season contribution of the real project fleet across regions.
why_it_matters: Peak adequacy is the binding planning constraint; CEMs need defensible firm-capacity inputs.
can_public_data_investigate: NOT for formal ELCC (no public hourly load, no outage data). Yes for bounded, scenario-labelled peak-window contribution using modelled output and explicit peak-hour assumptions, checked against monthly regional maxima.
confidence: Medium-high that formal ELCC is infeasible; medium that bounded approach is novel
verdict: Retain only in narrowed, explicitly-bounded form

what_literature_establishes: Temperature-demand links established nationally (hourly 2011-2015, non-public) and regionally for annual energy. PV-peak coincidence often assumed (L19) or shown for one city (L20) or with national load (L18).
what_remains_unresolved: Whether regional monthly peaks co-move with temperature in ways that modelled PV/wind output at actual project sites tracks or misses (e.g. summer heat reduces PV efficiency while raising load).
why_it_matters: Determines whether solar-heavy deployment helps where peaks are most climate-sensitive.
can_public_data_investigate: Partly: monthly regional max load + reanalysis temperature + modelled PV at project coordinates. Hourly coincidence cannot be observed.

what_literature_establishes: Optimisation studies show storage needed for night demand at high solar shares; CEM battery deployment sensitive to RE firm-capacity assumptions.
what_remains_unresolved: Public-data, region-specific evidence of storage duration needed to firm peak contribution.
why_it_matters: Storage procurement in KSA is under way; sizing evidence matters.
can_public_data_investigate: Only as clearly-labelled scenarios; no observed hourly net load.
verdict: Secondary; include only as a sensitivity (e.g. storage duration that would make modelled output cover a stated evening peak window)

what_literature_establishes: Studies rarely state what their data resolution can and cannot support; some assume coincidence.
what_remains_unresolved: A formal mapping of which adequacy-related claims are identifiable from annual, monthly and hourly public data.
why_it_matters: Prevents over-claiming from capacity-to-peak ratios; transferable to other data-poor systems.
can_public_data_investigate: Yes - this is precisely what the available public data allow.
verdict: Strong framing device; recommended as an explicit contribution

what_literature_establishes: Press reports of the KAPSARC tracker already disagree on solar share (76% vs 81% of 63.8 GW). GEM flags approximate coordinates.
what_remains_unresolved: Reconciliation of project databases (identity, status, capacity, coordinates) and its effect on regional metrics.
why_it_matters: Regional alignment results can flip if a few GW-scale projects are misassigned.
verdict: Include as a robustness layer; possible companion data paper
